v1.feedback: The boomerang concept lands — particles sweep out along curved arcs and return, which is a legible read on the 'swerve' brief. The warm-to-cool palette shift during flight is a nice touch and genuinely restrained. Two issues: the throw distance (10–18 units) risks pushing particles well outside frame on smaller viewports, and the 8-second fixed cycle with a hard sine envelope makes the return feel mechanical rather than surprising. A refined version should ease the return with a slower asymmetric envelope (fast throw, lazy drift back), tighten max throw distance to ~60% of current so Lucy's silhouette never fully dissolves, and consider a slight camera pull-back or FOV widen during peak dispersion so particles stay in frame.

v2.feedback: The boomerang reads as a radial explosion-and-return rather than a coherent directional throw — a true boomerang should fling the cloud in one dominant direction with a curved return arc, not scatter particles outward uniformly from the centroid. During peak throw the Lucy silhouette dissolves entirely into ambient scatter, losing the recognizable form for ~2s; consider clamping participation so a skeletal ghost of the figure persists at apex. The warm→cool palette shift is tasteful but subtle enough to miss on first cycle — push the slate-blue harder at peak or add a single accent hue on the leading wave-front to make the swerve legible as a deliberate event.
